name: NHPC Ltd.
business_summary: Government of India's flagship hydropower company (Navratna): 9,333 MW operating (8,771 MW hydro, 562 MW solar/wind; ~16.9% of India's hydro), 9,204 MW under construction (Subansiri Lower 2,000 MW being commissioned unit by unit, Parbati-II, Teesta-VI, Kiru, Kwar, Ratle, Dibang, Pakal Dul), ~10 GW awaiting clearances. Tariffs are CERC cost-plus with ~15.5% RoE on regulated equity, so earnings track capacity commissioning. Q2 FY27: revenue Rs 4,483 cr (+33%), net profit Rs 1,658 cr (+36%; consolidated +52%) after a Rs 231 cr Teesta IV provision. Promoter (President of India) 61.4%; mcap Rs 81.5k cr, P/E 18.8, dividend yield 2.0%; borrowings Rs 57.4k cr.

revenue_mix.geography: India (J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Assam/Arunachal, etc.)

exposures.mechanism: Regulated cost-plus hydro (CERC 15.5% RoE on regulated equity; equity base growing with ~Rs 9.2k cr of projects under construction): a bond-proxy with 2.0% dividend yield and P/E 18.8, EV/MCap ~1.6 (borrowings Rs 57.4k cr vs mcap Rs 81.5k cr). +25bp on a ~9% discount rate with duration ~9 => -2.2%; RoE not indexed to yields until the next tariff period => -2.0.

evidence.note: Mcap Rs 81,475 cr, P/E 18.8, div yield 2.0%, borrowings Rs 57,408 cr
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Interest on normative debt is a pass-through in CERC tariffs, so operating plants are insulated; exposure is interest during construction on Rs 38.9k cr CWIP (capitalised, raising project cost and delaying RoE) and floating-rate debt: Rs 57k cr x ~50% floating x 25bp = Rs 72 cr, ~70% recovered => Rs 22 cr = -0.5% of PAT, capitalised, EV/MCap 1.6 => -0.5.

evidence.note: Debt-equity ratio 1.16; long-term debt Rs 47,705 cr (Jun-26)
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: AAA PSU with government support, so spread beta is low; but incremental borrowing of Rs 15,000 cr FY27 capex (company target) is mostly debt-funded at 70:30. +50bp on ~Rs 10k cr = Rs 50 cr/yr, 70% passed through for operating assets, higher for CWIP => -0.8.

evidence.note: SolarQuarter: NHPC targets Rs 15,000 cr capex for FY27

exposures.mechanism: Revenue is largely capacity-based (PAF) under CERC tariffs, but generation above design energy earns secondary energy and PAF incentives (NHPC FY26: ~5% of revenue) and flood/silt events cut availability (Teesta V restoration completed; Teesta IV/Subansiri geological issues). A +10% rainfall year adds ~3-4% generation => ~+1.5% EBITDA, x1.6 EV/MCap x 0.35 persistence => +0.8; wide range because heavy rain also causes outages. Q2 FY27 with a 13% monsoon deficit still posted +33% revenue, driven by new capacity (Subansiri).

evidence.note: Subansiri Lower highest generation in Q1 FY27 (1,316 MU); Teesta-V restoration completed
Revenue +33% in Q2 on new hydro capacity (CNBC TV18 headline)

exposures.mechanism: Customers are state discoms; trade receivables Rs 4,354 cr (Jun-26) vs Rs 2,629 cr at Mar-26 and debtor days improved from 114 to 83 (screener). The LPS rules and discom reform improve collection and reduce working-capital interest; +1 SSU => debtor days -10 => +Rs 600 cr cash (0.7% of mcap) + risk premium cut => +2.5.

evidence.note: Trade receivables Rs 4,354 cr at Jun-26 vs Rs 2,629 cr at Mar-26

exposures.mechanism: Large hydro counts as renewable; pumped-storage VGF/ISTS waiver/hydro cost-overrun support improve the pipeline (10,263 MW awaiting clearances; 8,014 MW hydro under construction; 17,930 MW PSP under survey). Kamala (1,720 MW) got CCEA approval 8 Apr 2026 and is seeking forest clearance for 23.4 lakh trees (Oct). +1 SSU => +10% accelerated approvals => +2.5.

evidence.note: Hydro under construction 8,014 MW; awaiting clearances 10,118 MW; Kamala 1,720 MW CCEA approval 8.4.2026
NHPC seeks forest clearance to fell 23.4 lakh trees for Kamala; Sawalkot 1,856 MW work to start (Sep)

exposures.mechanism: PAF-based fixed charges make NHPC volume-insensitive; demand matters via secondary energy, peaking value of hydro and merchant sales, and sentiment for PSU generators. +3pp => +0.6.

evidence.note: Tariffs on availability (PAF) basis; secondary energy and PAF incentive small

exposures.mechanism: Central budgetary support for enabling infrastructure of hydro projects (roads/bridges, Rs 12-15k cr scheme - model knowledge) and equity infusion/PSU capex push lowers NHPC's net project cost. +10% government capex => +1.0.

evidence.note: Government pushing Sawalkot 1,856 MW, Etalin 3,097 MW, Kamala - approvals/MoUs

exposures.mechanism: Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance since 2025 (model knowledge; NatStrat Sep 2026 headline) accelerates NHPC's Chenab projects (Sawalkot, Pakal Dul, Kiru, Kwar, Ratle); escalation also raises attack/availability risk at Salal, Uri and J&K assets and cost overruns (4 J&K projects: Rs 5,737 cr overrun, 3.5-yr average delay - Rajya Sabha, 20 Jul 2026). Net slight positive, very wide range.

evidence.note: 4 strategic J&K hydro projects face Rs 5,737 cr cost overrun, avg 3.5 yr delay (PSU Watch)
After Abeyance: Indus Basin and the New Water Politics (NatStrat)

exposures.mechanism: Hydro construction uses steel (penstock, gates) and cement; project costs are approved in tariff but overruns beyond approved cost need CERC clearance and delay RoE. +7% steel on ~Rs 9k cr of annual capex x 10% steel content = Rs 63 cr, 40% unrecoverable => -0.03% mcap x 1.6... plus cost-overrun risk => -0.4. Pack shows +3.48 for iron ore (t +2.0), a spurious PSU/commodity-cycle co-movement not carried into the weight.

evidence.note: Projects under construction 9,204 MW with cost-overrun/geology issues (Teesta-IV provision Rs 231 cr in Q2)
Pack empirical F_IRON_ORE +3.48 per SSU, t +2.0

exposures.mechanism: FIIs 13.2% (up from 10.3% in Mar-26), DIIs 14.3%, promoter (Government) 61.4% after a ~6pp stake sale in Q1 FY27 (67.4% -> 61.4% per screener; OFS details not fetched); market beta ~1.2. +5bn => +1.5.
Pumped storage (17.9 GW under survey), solar (1,190 MW under construction), BESS and green-hydrogen optionality; 50,000 MW capacity target by 2047 (AGM, 28 Aug 2026). +1 SSU => +1.5.

evidence.note: NHPC 50th AGM targets 50,000 MW by 2047 (Sarkaritel headline)
